dedupe_keys.name: maximisation of open hospital capacity under shortage of sars cov 2 vaccines stochastic simulation tool excel vba

description: This spreadsheet tool simulates how a hospital should vaccinate its staff when vaccine doses are scarce, so that as much of the hospital as possible stays open during a COVID-19 wave. The producers are Wolfram Bosbach of the University of Giessen in Germany with Heinrich, Kolisch and Heiss, who published it as an open-access stochastic simulation tool alongside a 2021 article in the journal Vaccines. The model represents groups of hospital staff whose infection causes absences that close wards, and compares strategies for allocating a limited number of doses over time, running random draws to show the spread of outcomes. Coverage is a single hospital whose parameters the user sets. The Excel workbook with its VBA macro is available as a free download from Zenodo under the GNU General Public License version 2 or later. Caveats: written for the early 2021 vaccine shortage, it needs Excel with macros enabled, and parameters must be adapted to each hospital. Simulation uses: estimating how staff absence in an epidemic reduces open hospital capacity, and prioritising protective measures for the workforce that keeps critical services running. Related records: the Augsburg nursing staff data (data-augsburg-nursing-staff-capacity) give observed absences, and Covasim (model-covasim) simulates epidemic spread.
inputs: Hospital staff groups and their infection and absence risks
Number of vaccine doses available over time
name: Maximisation of open hospital capacity under shortage of SARS-CoV-2 vaccines: stochastic simulation tool (Excel VBA)
outputs: Share of hospital capacity that stays open over time under each strategy
provider: Wolfram A. Bosbach (University of Giessen) with M. Heinrich, R. Kolisch and C. Heiss
